key_insight: Ternary blending can improve both voltage tuning and spectral coverage in RAINBOW organic solar cells, enabling higher-efficiency 2- and 3-junction architectures without stacked-device current matching constraints.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that side-by-side, externally connected multijunction OPVs can be fabricated with scalable blade coating and optimized through material blending plus device simulation for practical efficiency gains.
method: Screened 7 binary active layers spanning 1.98 to 1.16 eV bandgaps.
Evaluated 5 ternary blends to address losses in the widest- and narrowest-gap subcells.
Built and simulated 2-junction and 3-junction RAINBOW devices using meniscus-guided blade-coated subcells.
evidence_signal: Proof-of-concept devices improved from 12.9% single-junction efficiency to 15.9% for 2-junction devices and 17.3% for 3-junction devices, with simulations predicting 16.4% and 17.7% respectively.
watch_item: The approach still depends on finding high-efficiency wide-bandgap materials in the 2.0–2.5 eV range, which remains a key materials bottleneck.
paper_title: Exploring the Potential of Ternary Blending for Two and Three-Junction RAINBOW Solar Cells
